opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Edward Fleming (E042) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees can have up to write; Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. Write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E042 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists E042 as full-time (max write), while the Security database lists E042 as a contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training). Given conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive policy, which caps access at read. The requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, so I grant the maximum permitted: read.
